Trucks engulfed in flames after crash on WA highway

A refrigerated truck and a truck towing a container trailer catch fire after crashing in Western Australia’s Wheatbelt, with emergency services on the scene.

Topic:Accidents and Emergency Incidents

The charred remains of the two trucks after firefighters extinguished the blaze.  (ABC News )

Two trucks have caught fire after a crash in Western Australia’s Wheatbelt, with emergency services on the scene.

The crash between a refrigerated truck and a truck towing a container trailer was reported about 6.45am at the intersection of Great Eastern Highway and Quellington Road in Meckering, about 130 kilometres from Perth.

A Department of Fire and Emergency Services (DFES) spokesperson said both vehicles were engulfed in flames when crews arrived around 7am.

The fiery crash saw a thick black plume of smoke spilling into the sky. (Supplied)

It is understood the blaze has since been extinguished.

Nine volunteer and career firefighting crews and four ambulance crews had been sent to the scene, and the emergency helicopter dispatched.

The helicopter has since been stood down but fire crews remain at the scene.

It is not known how many people are involved.

Aerial vision from the scene shows the charred and mangled wreckage of the refrigerated truck strewn across the road as firefighters continue to hose it down.

The crash involved a refrigerated truck and a truck towing a container trailer.  (ABC News )

A large area of charred ground can be seen adjacent to the road.

Traffic is banked up in the area, and there are multiple police cars and fire trucks lining the road near the crash.

Great Eastern Highway remains closed near Quellington Road, with drivers advised to seek an alternate route.

Firefighters have extinguished the blaze.  (ABC News )

Police are urging anyone with information contact Crime Stoppers.
